verses.sanskrit: क्रोधं न गच्छत्यापन्नः प्रियं न वदते मृषा | नाददाते अनृतेनार्थं पण्डितो लक्षणं त्रयम् ||
verses.transliteration: krodhaṃ na gacchatyāpannaḥ priyaṃ na vadate mṛṣā | nādadāte anṛtenārthaṃ paṇḍito lakṣaṇaṃ trayam ||
verses.translation: One who does not fall into anger when afflicted, who does not speak falsehood to please, who does not acquire wealth through untruth — these are the three marks of the pandit.
verses.hindi: जो आपद में भी क्रोध नहीं करता, प्रिय लगने के लिए झूठ नहीं बोलता, और असत्य से धन नहीं लेता — ये पण्डित के तीन लक्षण हैं।
verses.commentary: Vidura's three-fold definition of wisdom is entirely behavioral — not philosophical knowledge but behavioral integrity under pressure. (1) "Āpannaḥ krodhaṃ na gacchati" — does not fall into anger when afflicted. Anger under difficulty is the easiest response; not reacting with anger when legitimately wronged is the mark of genuine equanimity. (2) "Priyaṃ na vadate mṛṣā" — does not speak falsehood to please. The temptation to say what the other person wants to hear (flattery, false comfort, agreement with what one knows is wrong) is one of the most common forms of dishonesty. The pandit chooses truth over social ease. (3) "Anṛtena arthaṃ nādadāte" — does not acquire wealth through untruth. The integration of ethics and livelihood: means matter, not just ends. All three marks appear specifically under pressure — when anger would be understandable, when a lie would be convenient, when dishonesty would be profitable.

verses.sanskrit: आरभते न कर्माणि भयाद्योऽल्पफलानि च | अश्रद्धयालसो नित्यं स मूढो भरतर्षभ ||
verses.transliteration: ārabhate na karmāṇi bhayādyo'lpaphalāni ca | aśraddhayālaso nityaṃ sa mūḍho bharatarṣabha ||
verses.translation: One who does not begin actions out of fear, or because the fruit seems small; who is always without faith and lazy — O best of the Bharatas, that one is the mudha (fool).
verses.hindi: जो भय से काम नहीं आरंभ करता, जो अल्पफल समझकर नहीं करता; जो सदा श्रद्धाहीन और आलसी है — वह मूढ है, हे भरतश्रेष्ठ!
verses.commentary: Vidura defines the mudha (fool) not by lack of intelligence but by three specific failure modes: (1) "Bhayāt na ārabhate" — does not begin because of fear. The fear of failure, criticism, or effort prevents action — the most common form of self-sabotage. (2) "Alpaphalāni na karoti" — does not act because the result seems small. The fool measures everything by immediate, visible reward and ignores small consistent actions that compound into large outcomes. (3) "Aśraddhayā ālasaḥ" — without faith and lazy. Lacking belief in the value of the work or in one's own capacity, combined with the resulting inertia. The mudha is not stupid — they are paralyzed by fear, impatience, and faithlessness. This is a more accurate description of most human underperformance than any theory of fixed intelligence.

verses.sanskrit: अनागतं यः कुरुते स पण्डितो | दैवाहतं नैव विचिन्तयेत् तु | कालं प्रतीक्षन् कृतसंनिवेशो | नित्यं जयत्यर्थकृते प्रयत्नात् ||
verses.transliteration: anāgataṃ yaḥ kurute sa paṇḍito | daivāhataṃ naiva vicintayet tu | kālaṃ pratīkṣan kṛtasaṃniveśo | nityaṃ jayatyarthakṛte prayatnāt ||
verses.translation: One who prepares for what has not yet come is the pandit. One who does not grieve over what fate has destroyed; who waits for the right time with steady preparation — such a person always succeeds through effort toward the goal.
verses.hindi: जो भविष्य के लिए तैयारी करता है वह पण्डित है। जो भाग्य ने जो नष्ट किया उस पर शोक नहीं करता; जो सही समय की प्रतीक्षा करता हुआ सदा तैयार रहता है — वह प्रयत्न से सफल होता है।
verses.commentary: The pandit's relationship with time: three components. (1) "Anāgataṃ yaḥ kurute" — prepares for what has not yet arrived. Proactive preparation — not reactive scrambling. The pandit does not wait for the crisis to prepare; they prepare before the crisis. (2) "Daivāhataṃ naiva vicintayet" — does not grieve what fate has destroyed. What is gone is gone. The energy spent in grief over irreversible loss is energy not available for the present. (3) "Kālaṃ pratīkṣan kṛtasaṃniveśaḥ" — awaits the right time while remaining in prepared readiness. Patient timing combined with continuous preparation — not passive waiting but active preparation during a fallow period. The integration: prepare before, release after, stay ready during. "Nityaṃ jayati" — always succeeds.

verses.sanskrit: योगश्चित्तवृत्तिरोधो योगो मोक्षप्रदायकः | योगः सर्वबन्धानां योगो धर्मसमाश्रयः ||
verses.transliteration: yogaścittavṛttirodho yogo mokṣapradāyakaḥ | yogaḥ sarvabandhānāṃ yogaḥ dharmasamāśrayaḥ ||
verses.translation: Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications; yoga gives liberation. Yoga cuts all bonds; yoga rests on dharma.
verses.hindi: योग चित्त-वृत्तियों का निरोध है; योग मोक्ष देता है। योग सभी बंधनों को काटता है; योग धर्म पर आश्रित है।
verses.commentary: The definition of yoga from Yoga Sutras, placed in the context of dharma. Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications, leading to liberation. All bonds are cut through this practice, which rests on the foundation of dharma.
verses.wordMeaning: The definition of yoga from Yoga Sutras, placed in the context of dharma. Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications, leading to liberation. All bonds are cut through this practice, which rests on the foundation of dharma.

verses.sanskrit: अहं ब्रह्मास्मि न त्वं भूतिर्न च भूतानि | सर्वं धर्म एव सर्वं धर्म मयि सर्वम् ||
verses.transliteration: ahaṃ brahmāsmi na tvaṃ bhūtirna ca bhūtāni | sarvaṃ dharma eva sarvaṃ dharma mayi sarvam ||
verses.translation: I am Brahman, not you; I am birth, not beings; all is dharma alone, all is dharma in me.
verses.hindi: मैं ब्रह्म हूँ, तुम नहीं; मैं जन्म हूँ, प्राणी नहीं; सब धर्म ही है, सब धर्म मेरे में है।
verses.commentary: The declaration of non-duality with dharma as the supreme. The individual Self is Brahman; the world is dharma; all distinctions dissolve in this recognition.
verses.wordMeaning: The declaration of non-duality with dharma as the supreme. The individual Self is Brahman; the world is dharma; all distinctions dissolve in this recognition.

verses.sanskrit: यथा नदी समुद्रेषु यथा दीपो दीतेषु | तथा जीवो धर्मे लीनो न तत्र संशयो भवति ||
verses.transliteration: yathā nadī samudreṣu yathā dīpo dīpiteṣu | tathā jīvo dharme līno na tatra saṃśayo bhavati ||
verses.translation: As rivers merge into the ocean, as lamps merge into light — so the individual self merges into dharma. There is no doubt about this.
verses.hindi: जैसे नदियाँ समुद्र में लीन हो जाती हैं, जैसे दीप ज्योति में लीन हो जाते हैं — वैसे ही जीव धर्म में लीन हो जाता है। इसमें कोई संशय नहीं।
verses.commentary: The dissolution of individuality into dharma. The images of rivers into ocean and lamps into light illustrate the loss of separate identity while the essence remains.
verses.wordMeaning: The dissolution of individuality into dharma. The images of rivers into ocean and lamps into light illustrate the loss of separate identity while the essence remains.

verses.sanskrit: शान्तं शिवमद्वैतं धर्म नित्यं शुद्धमच्युतम् | यो जानाति स पश्यति यो न जानाति न पश्यति ||
verses.transliteration: śāntaṃ śivamadvaitaṃ dharma nityaṃ śuddhamacyutam | yo jānāti sa paśyati yo na jānāti na paśyati ||
verses.translation: Peaceful, auspicious, non-dual dharma — eternal, pure, immutable. He who knows, sees; he who does not know, does not see.
verses.hindi: शांत, शिव, अद्वैत धर्म — नित्य, शुद्ध, अच्युत। जो जानता है, वह देखता है; जो नहीं जानता, वह नहीं देखता।
verses.commentary: The attributes of dharma: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.
verses.wordMeaning: The attributes of dharma: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.

verses.sanskrit: एको देवो द्वितीयो नास्ति यो धर्मं वेद तत्त्वतः | सोऽहमस्मि न किंचिद्भूतो न मृत्युर्न शोको न तथा ||
verses.transliteration: eko devo dvitīyo nāsti yo dharmaṃ veda tattvataḥ | so'hamasmi na kiñcidbhūto na mṛtyurna śoko na tathā ||
verses.translation: There is one God, no second — he who knows dharma in truth. I am He, not any being, no death, no sorrow, and so on.
verses.hindi: एक ही देव है, दूसरा कोई नहीं — जो धर्म को तत्व से जानता है। मैं वही हूँ, कोई प्राणी नहीं, मृत्यु नहीं, शोक नहीं, वगैरह।
verses.commentary: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.
verses.wordMeaning: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.

chapters.title: Pandit Lakshana — The Marks of the Wise

verses.sanskrit: न ब्रूयात् सत्यमप्रियम् | प्रियं च नानृतं ब्रूयात् | एष धर्मः सनातनः ||
verses.transliteration: na brūyāt satyamapriyam | priyaṃ ca nānṛtaṃ brūyāt | eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ ||
verses.translation: Do not speak truth that is cruel. And do not speak falsehood that is pleasing. This is the eternal dharma.
verses.hindi: अप्रिय सत्य न बोलो। और प्रिय असत्य भी न बोलो। यही सनातन धर्म है।
verses.commentary: The most precise ethical formulation in all of Sanskrit literature on speech. Vidura draws two boundaries: (1) "Satyam apriyam na brūyāt" — do not speak truth that wounds needlessly. Truth without compassion is cruelty disguised as honesty. The timing, tone, and context of truth-telling determine whether it helps or harms. (2) "Priyam anṛtam na brūyāt" — do not speak falsehood that pleases. Comfortable lies — telling people what they want to hear — are still lies, and ultimately serve neither the speaker nor the listener. The space between these two prohibitions is the zone of genuine communication: truth spoken with care for its effect, honesty calibrated to the listener's capacity to receive it. "Eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ" — this is the eternal dharma. Not a rule but a principle: speech that is both true and kind.

verses.sanskrit: षडेते नरकद्वाराः प्राणिनां दुर्गतिप्रदाः | आलस्यं तन्द्रा भयं क्रोधः आशा दीर्घसूत्रता ||
verses.transliteration: ṣaḍete narakadvārāḥ prāṇināṃ durgatiPradāḥ | ālasyaṃ tandrā bhayaṃ krodhaḥ āśā dīrghasūtratā ||
verses.translation: These six are the gates of hell that lead beings toward ruin: laziness, drowsiness, fear, anger, false hope, and procrastination (dīrghasūtratā — long-threadedness).
verses.hindi: ये छः प्राणियों के नरक के द्वार और दुर्गति के कारण हैं: आलस्य, तन्द्रा (उनींदापन), भय, क्रोध, आशा (मिथ्या आशा) और दीर्घसूत्रता (काम को टालते रहना)।
verses.commentary: Vidura's six gates of ruin — each precise in its diagnosis: (1) Ālasya (laziness): the refusal to engage with what requires effort. (2) Tandrā (drowsiness/dullness): the mental torpor that prevents clear perception. (3) Bhaya (fear): the paralysis that prevents necessary action. (4) Krodha (anger): the reactive state that destroys good judgment and relationships. (5) Āśā (false hope): the passive waiting for things to improve without corresponding action — hope as avoidance. (6) Dīrghasūtratā (procrastination, "long-threadedness"): stretching a thread longer and longer — the tendency to always have one more step before beginning. These six are gates — they do not slam shut suddenly but are entered gradually, one step at a time. The word "narakadvārāḥ" — gates of hell — means these produce a hellish quality of life, not necessarily a cosmological destination.

verses.sanskrit: यस्य कृत्यं न जानन्ति मन्त्रं वा गुह्यमेव वा | कृतमेवास्य जानन्ति स वै पण्डित उच्यते ||
verses.transliteration: yasya kṛtyaṃ na jānanti mantraṃ vā guhyameva vā | kṛtamevāsya jānanti sa vai paṇḍita ucyate ||
verses.translation: One whose plans no one knows, whose counsel and secrets are hidden — and whose actions are known only when they are done — that one is truly called a pandit.
verses.hindi: जिसके कार्य को कोई नहीं जानता, जिसकी मंत्रणा और गुप्त बात छुपी रहती है — और जिसके काम को लोग तभी जानते हैं जब वह हो जाता है — वह पण्डित कहलाता है।
verses.commentary: Vidura's counsel on strategic silence. The pandit does not announce plans before they are executed. Three reasons: (1) Premature announcement invites interference — opposition that might not have materialized has time to organize. (2) The energy of intention dissipates when spoken prematurely — psychological research on goal-sharing confirms that talking about a goal activates the same neural reward as achieving it, reducing motivation to actually do it. (3) The pandit is measured by results, not by impressions — "kṛtamevāsya jānanti" — they know only the done thing. This is the ethic of action over announcement. Vidura is not counseling secrecy for its own sake but the discipline of completing before claiming.

verses.transliteration: śāntaṃ śivamadvaitaṃ dharma nityaṃ śuddhamacyutam | yo jānāti sa paśyati yo na jānāti na paśyati ||
verses.translation: Peaceful, auspicious, non-dual dharma — eternal, pure, immutable. He who knows, sees; he who does not know, does not see.
verses.hindi: शांत, शिव, अद्वैत धर्म — नित्य, शुद्ध, अच्युत। जो जानता है, वह देखता है; जो नहीं जानता, वह नहीं देखता।
verses.commentary: The attributes of dharma: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.
verses.wordMeaning: The attributes of dharma: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.

verses.sanskrit: एको देवो द्वितीयो नास्ति यो धर्मं वेद तत्त्वतः | सोऽहमस्मि न किंचिद्भूतो न मृत्युर्न शोको न तथा ||
verses.transliteration: eko devo dvitīyo nāsti yo dharmaṃ veda tattvataḥ | so'hamasmi na kiñcidbhūto na mṛtyurna śoko na tathā ||
verses.translation: There is one God, no second — he who knows dharma in truth. I am He, not any being, no death, no sorrow, and so on.
verses.hindi: एक ही देव है, दूसरा कोई नहीं — जो धर्म को तत्व से जानता है। मैं वही हूँ, कोई प्राणी नहीं, मृत्यु नहीं, शोक नहीं, वगैरह।
verses.commentary: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.
verses.wordMeaning: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.

chapters.title: Niti Vakya — Governance and Practical Ethics

verses.sanskrit: प्रियस्य च पथ्यस्य च दुर्लभः श्रोता | अप्रियस्य च पथ्यस्य वक्ता श्रोता च दुर्लभौ ||
verses.transliteration: priyasya ca pathyasya ca durlabhaḥ śrotā | apriyasya ca pathyasya vaktā śrotā ca durlabhau ||
verses.translation: Rare is the listener for that which is both pleasant and beneficial. Even rarer are both the speaker and listener of that which is unpleasant yet beneficial.
verses.hindi: जो प्रिय भी हो और हितकर भी — उसका श्रोता दुर्लभ है। जो अप्रिय हो किन्तु हितकर हो — उसका वक्ता और श्रोता दोनों दुर्लभ हैं।
verses.commentary: Vidura's taxonomy of communication and its rarity. The ideal communication is "priya" (pleasant) AND "pathya" (beneficial) — even this is rare because most people avoid the beneficial when it is merely pleasant to receive but difficult to act on. The rarest category: "apriya pathya" — unpleasant but beneficial. Vidura himself is the apriya-pathya voice in the Mahabharata. He tells Dhritarashtra things that are uncomfortable to hear but necessary to act on. The tragedy: not only are speakers of such truth rare, but listeners are even rarer. Dhritarashtra is the model of the person who hears the apriya-pathya counsel and cannot act on it — because his attachment to his son Duryodhana overrides everything he intellectually knows to be right. The Vidura Niti is addressed to anyone who has this capacity: to hear what is difficult and act on it.
verses.wordMeaning: Vidura's taxonomy of communication and its rarity. The ideal communication is "priya" (pleasant) AND "pathya" (beneficial) — even this is rare because most people avoid the beneficial when it is merely pleasant to receive but difficult to act on. The rarest category: "apriya pathya" — unpleasant but beneficial. Vidura himself is the apriya-pathya voice in the Mahabharata. He tells Dhritarashtra things that are uncomfortable to hear but necessary to act on. The tragedy: not only are speakers of such truth rare, but listeners are even rarer. Dhritarashtra is the model of the person who hears the apriya-pathya counsel and cannot act on it — because his attachment to his son Duryodhana overrides everything he intellectually knows to be right. The Vidura Niti is addressed to anyone who has this capacity: to hear what is difficult and act on it.

verses.sanskrit: धर्म एव हतो हन्ति धर्मो रक्षति रक्षितः | तस्माद्धर्मो न हन्तव्यो मा नो धर्मो हतोऽवधीत् ||
verses.transliteration: dharma eva hato hanti dharmo rakṣati rakṣitaḥ | tasmāddharmo na hantavyo mā no dharmo hato'vadhīt ||
verses.translation: Dharma, when destroyed, destroys. Dharma, when protected, protects. Therefore dharma must not be destroyed, lest the destroyed dharma destroy us.
verses.hindi: धर्म नष्ट होने पर नष्ट करता है, रक्षित होने पर रक्षा करता है। इसलिए धर्म को नष्ट न करो, नहीं तो नष्ट किया हुआ धर्म हमें नष्ट करेगा।
verses.commentary: The most memorable verse of the Vidura Niti — and one of the most cited in the entire Mahabharata. The logical structure is elegant and unambiguous: dharma is not neutral. It is either protective or destructive depending on how it is treated. When you protect dharma (act rightly, maintain honesty, fulfill your obligations), dharma protects you — not through supernatural reward but through the natural consequence of trustworthy conduct: others trust you, systems function, relationships hold. When you violate dharma — compromise your integrity for short-term gain, use unjust means for just ends — the violation returns. The Mahabharata itself is the demonstration: Dhritarashtra's violation of dharma (tolerating Duryodhana's adharma) eventually destroys everything he tried to protect.
verses.wordMeaning: The most memorable verse of the Vidura Niti — and one of the most cited in the entire Mahabharata. The logical structure is elegant and unambiguous: dharma is not neutral. verses.sanskrit: योगश्चित्तवृत्तिरोधो योगो मोक्षप्रदायकः | योगः सर्वबन्धानां योगो धर्मसमाश्रयः ||
verses.transliteration: yogaścittavṛttirodho yogo mokṣapradāyakaḥ | yogaḥ sarvabandhānāṃ yogaḥ dharmasamāśrayaḥ ||
verses.translation: Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications; yoga gives liberation. Yoga cuts all bonds; yoga rests on dharma.
verses.hindi: योग चित्त-वृत्तियों का निरोध है; योग मोक्ष देता है। योग सभी बंधनों को काटता है; योग धर्म पर आश्रित है।
verses.commentary: The definition of yoga from Yoga Sutras, placed in the context of dharma. Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications, leading to liberation. All bonds are cut through this practice, which rests on the foundation of dharma.
verses.wordMeaning: The definition of yoga from Yoga Sutras, placed in the context of dharma. Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications, leading to liberation. All bonds are cut through this practice, which rests on the foundation of dharma.

verses.sanskrit: अहं ब्रह्मास्मि न त्वं भूतिर्न च भूतानि | सर्वं धर्म एव सर्वं धर्म मयि सर्वम् ||
verses.transliteration: ahaṃ brahmāsmi na tvaṃ bhūtirna ca bhūtāni | sarvaṃ dharma eva sarvaṃ dharma mayi sarvam ||
verses.translation: I am Brahman, not you; I am birth, not beings; all is dharma alone, all is dharma in me.
verses.hindi: मैं ब्रह्म हूँ, तुम नहीं; मैं जन्म हूँ, प्राणी नहीं; सब धर्म ही है, सब धर्म मेरे में है।
verses.commentary: The declaration of non-duality with dharma as the supreme. The individual Self is Brahman; the world is dharma; all distinctions dissolve in this recognition.
verses.wordMeaning: The declaration of non-duality with dharma as the supreme. The individual Self is Brahman; the world is dharma; all distinctions dissolve in this recognition.

verses.sanskrit: यथा नदी समुद्रेषु यथा दीपो दीतेषु | तथा जीवो धर्मे लीनो न तत्र संशयो भवति ||
verses.transliteration: yathā nadī samudreṣu yathā dīpo dīpiteṣu | tathā jīvo dharme līno na tatra saṃśayo bhavati ||
verses.translation: As rivers merge into the ocean, as lamps merge into light — so the individual self merges into dharma. There is no doubt about this.
verses.hindi: जैसे नदियाँ समुद्र में लीन हो जाती हैं, जैसे दीप ज्योति में लीन हो जाते हैं — वैसे ही जीव धर्म में लीन हो जाता है। इसमें कोई संशय नहीं।
verses.commentary: The dissolution of individuality into dharma. The images of rivers into ocean and lamps into light illustrate the loss of separate identity while the essence remains.
verses.wordMeaning: The dissolution of individuality into dharma. The images of rivers into ocean and lamps into light illustrate the loss of separate identity while the essence remains.

verses.sanskrit: शान्तं शिवमद्वैतं धर्म नित्यं शुद्धमच्युतम् | यो जानाति स पश्यति यो न जानाति न पश्यति ||
verses.transliteration: śāntaṃ śivamadvaitaṃ dharma nityaṃ śuddhamacyutam | yo jānāti sa paśyati yo na jānāti na paśyati ||
verses.translation: Peaceful, auspicious, non-dual dharma — eternal, pure, immutable. He who knows, sees; he who does not know, does not see.
verses.hindi: शांत, शिव, अद्वैत धर्म — नित्य, शुद्ध, अच्युत। जो जानता है, वह देखता है; जो नहीं जानता, वह नहीं देखता।
verses.commentary: The attributes of dharma: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.
verses.wordMeaning: The attributes of dharma: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.

verses.sanskrit: एको देवो द्वितीयो नास्ति यो धर्मं वेद तत्त्वतः | सोऽहमस्मि न किंचिद्भूतो न मृत्युर्न शोको न तथा ||
verses.transliteration: eko devo dvitīyo nāsti yo dharmaṃ veda tattvataḥ | so'hamasmi na kiñcidbhūto na mṛtyurna śoko na tathā ||
verses.translation: There is one God, no second — he who knows dharma in truth. I am He, not any being, no death, no sorrow, and so on.
verses.hindi: एक ही देव है, दूसरा कोई नहीं — जो धर्म को तत्व से जानता है। मैं वही हूँ, कोई प्राणी नहीं, मृत्यु नहीं, शोक नहीं, वगैरह।
verses.commentary: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.
verses.wordMeaning: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.

verses.sanskrit: अध्यायः ३६ विदुर उवाच । अत्रैवोदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् । आत्रेयस्य च संवादं साध्यानां चेति नः श्रुतम्
verses.transliteration: adhyAyaH 36 vidura uvAcha | atraivodAharantImamitihAsaM purAtanam | Atreyasya cha sa.nvAda.n sAdhyAnA.n cheti naH shrutam
verses.translation: "Vidura said, 'In this connection is cited the old story of the discourse between the son of Atri and the deities called Sadhyas is as heard by us.
verses.hindi: धृतराष्ट्रका भेजा हुआ बह दूत जाकर विदुर्से बोला---“महामते ! हमारे स्वामी महाराज धृतराष्ट्र आपसे मिलना चाहते हैं
verses.wordMeaning: "Vidura said, 'In this connection is cited the old story of the discourse between the son of Atri and the deities called Sadhyas is as heard by us.
verses.commentary: Sense: "Vidura said, 'In this connection is cited the old story of the discourse between the son of Atri and the deities called Sadhyas is as heard by us.

verses.sanskrit: चरन्तं हंसरूपेण महर्षिं संशितव्रतम् । साध्या देवा महाप्राज्ञं पर्यपृच्छन्त वै पुरा
verses.transliteration: charanta.n ha.nsarUpeNa maharShiM saMshitavratam | sAdhyA devA mahAprAj~naM paryapR^ichChanta vai purA
verses.translation: In days of old, the deities known by the name of Sadhyas questioned the highly wise and great Rishi of rigid vows (the son of Atri), while the latter was wandering in the guise of one depending on eleemosynary charity for livelihood. The Sadhyas said, 'We are, O great Rishi, deities known as Sadhyas. Beholding thee, we are unable to guess who thou art. It seemeth to us, however, that thou art possessed of intelligence and self-control in consequence of acquaintance with the scriptures. It, therefore, behoveth thee to discourse to us in magnanimous words fraught with learning.'
verses.hindi: उसके ऐसा कहनेपर विदुरजी राजमहलके पास जाकर बोले---'द्वारपाल !: धृतराष्ट्रको मेरे आनेकी सूचना दें दो'
verses.wordMeaning: In days of old, the deities known by the name of Sadhyas questioned the highly wise and great Rishi of rigid vows (the son of Atri), while the latter was wandering in the guise of one depending on eleemosynary charity for livelihood. The Sadhyas said, 'We are, O great Rishi,…
verses.commentary: Sense: In days of old, the deities known by the name of Sadhyas questioned the highly wise and great Rishi of rigid vows (the son of Atri), while the latter was wandering in the guise of one depending on eleemosynary charity for livelihood. The Sadhyas said, 'We are, O great Rishi,…

verses.sanskrit: साध्या ऊचुः । साध्या देवा वय्मस्मो महर्षे दृष्ट्वा भवन्तं न शक्नुमोऽनुमातुम् । श्रुतेन धीरो बुद्धिमांस्त्वं मतो नः काव्यां वाचं वक्तुमर्हस्युदाराम्
verses.transliteration: sAdhyA UchuH | sAdhyA devA vaymasmo maharShe dR^iShTvA bhavantaM na shaknumo.anumAtum | shrutena dhIro buddhimA.nstvaM mato naH kAvyA.n vAchaM vaktumarhasyudArAm
verses.translation: "Vidura said, 'In this connection is cited the old story of the discourse between the son of Atri and the deities called Sadhyas is as heard by us. In days of old, the deities known by the name of Sadhyas questioned the highly wise and great Rishi of rigid vows (the son of Atri), while the latter was wandering in the guise of one depending on eleemosynary charity for livelihood.
verses.hindi: धृतराष्ट्रने कहा--'महाबुद्धिमान्‌ दूरदर्शी विदुरको भीतर ले आओ, मुझे इस विदुरसे मिलनेमें कभी भी अड़चन नहीं है!
verses.wordMeaning: "Vidura said, 'In this connection is cited the old story of the discourse between the son of Atri and the deities called Sadhyas is as heard by us. In days of old,…
verses.commentary: Sense: "Vidura said, 'In this connection is cited the old story of the discourse between the son of Atri and the deities called Sadhyas is as heard by us. In days of old,…

verses.sanskrit: हंस उवाच । एतत्कार्यममराः संश्रुतं मे धृतिः शमः सत्यधर्मानुवृत्तिः । ग्रन्थिं विनीय हृदयस्य सर्वं प्रियाप्रिये चात्मवशं नयीत
verses.transliteration: ha.nsa uvAcha | etatkAryamamarAH saMshrutaM me dhR^itiH shamaH satyadharmAnuvR^ittiH | granthi.n vinIya hR^idayasya sarvaM priyApriye chAtmavashaM nayIta
verses.translation: The mendicant Rishi answered, 'Ye immortals, it hath been heard by me that by untying all the knots in the heart by the aid of tranquillity, and by mastery over all the passions, and observance of true religion, one should regard both the agreeable and the disagreeable like his own self.
verses.hindi: द्वारपाल बविदुरके पास आकर बोल्ला-- विदुरजी ! आप बुद्धिमान्‌ महाराज धृतराष्ट्रके अन्तःपुरमें प्रवेश कीजिये। महाराजने मुझसे कहा है कि मुझे बिदुस्से मिलनेमें कभी अड़चन नहीं है'
verses.wordMeaning: The mendicant Rishi answered, 'Ye immortals, it hath been heard by me that by untying all the knots in the heart by the aid of tranquillity, and by mastery over all the passions, and observance of true religion,…
verses.commentary: Sense: The mendicant Rishi answered, 'Ye immortals, it hath been heard by me that by untying all the knots in the heart by the aid of tranquillity, and by mastery over all the passions, and observance of true religion,…

verses.sanskrit: आक्रुश्यमानो नाक्रोशेन्मन्युरेव तितिक्षितः । आक्रोष्टारं निर्दहति सुकृतं चास्य विन्दति
verses.transliteration: AkrushyamAno nAkroshenmanyureva titixitaH | AkroShTAraM nirdahati sukR^ita.n chAsya vindati
verses.translation: One should not return the slanders or reproaches of others for the pain that is felt by him who beareth silently, consumeth the slanderer; and he that beareth, succeedeth also in appropriating the virtues of the slanderer.
verses.hindi: वैशम्पायनजी कहते हैं--तदनन्तर विदुर धृतराष्ट्रे महलके भीतर जाकर चिन्तामें पड़े हुए राजासे हाथ जोड़कर बोलें---
verses.wordMeaning: One should not return the slanders or reproaches of others for the pain that is felt by him who beareth silently, consumeth the slanderer; and he that beareth, succeedeth also in appropriating the virtues of the slanderer.
verses.commentary: Sense: One should not return the slanders or reproaches of others for the pain that is felt by him who beareth silently, consumeth the slanderer; and he that beareth, succeedeth also in appropriating the virtues of the slanderer.

verses.sanskrit: नाक्रोशी स्यान्नावमानी परस्य मित्रद्रोही नोत नीचोपसेवी । न चातिमानी न च हीनवृत्तो रूक्षां वाचं रुशतीं वर्जयीत
verses.transliteration: nAkroshI syAnnAvamAnI parasya mitradrohI nota nIchopasevI | na chAtimAnI na cha hInavR^itto rUxA.n vAchaM rushatIM varjayIta
verses.translation: Indulge not in slanders and reproaches. Do not humiliate and insult others. Quarrel not with friends. Abstain from companionship with those that are vile and low. Be not arrogant and ignoble in conduct. Avoid words that are harsh and fraught with anger.
verses.hindi: धृतराष्ट्रने कहा--विदुर ! बुद्धिमान्‌ संजय आया था, मुझे बुरा-भल्त कहकर चला गया है। करू सभामें वह अजातशात्रु युधिष्ठिरके वचन खुनायेगा
verses.wordMeaning: Indulge not in slanders and reproaches. Do not humiliate and insult others. Quarrel not with friends. Abstain from companionship with those that are vile and low. Be not arrogant and ignoble in conduct. Avoid words that are harsh and fraught with anger.
verses.commentary: Sense: Indulge not in slanders and reproaches. Do not humiliate and insult others. Quarrel not with friends. Abstain from companionship with those that are vile and low. Be not arrogant and ignoble in conduct. Avoid words that are harsh and fraught with anger.

verses.sanskrit: मर्माण्यस्थीनि हृदयं तथासून् घोरा वाचो निर्दहन्तीह पुंसाम् । तस्माद्वाचं रुशतीं रूक्षरूपां धर्मारामो नित्यशो वर्जयीत
verses.transliteration: marmANyasthIni hR^idaya.n tathAsUn.h ghorA vAcho nirdahantIha pu.nsAm | tasmAdvAcha.n rushatIM rUxarUpAM dharmArAmo nityasho varjayIta
verses.translation: Harsh words burn and scorch the very vitals, bones, heart, and the very sources of the life of men. Therefore, he, that is virtuous, should always abstain from harsh and angry words.
verses.hindi: आज मैं उस कुरुवीर युधिष्ठिरकी बात न जान सका--चही मेंरे अज्जोंको जल्ज रहा है और इसीने मुझे अबतक जगा रखा है
verses.wordMeaning: Harsh words burn and scorch the very vitals, bones, heart, and the very sources of the life of men. Therefore, he, that is virtuous, should always abstain from harsh and angry words.
verses.commentary: Sense: Harsh words burn and scorch the very vitals, bones, heart, and the very sources of the life of men. Therefore, he, that is virtuous, should always abstain from harsh and angry words.

verses.sanskrit: अरुं तुरं परुषं रूक्षवाचं वाक्कण्टकैर्वितुदन्तं मनुष्यान् । विद्यादलक्ष्मीकतमं जनानां मुखे निबद्धां निरृतिं वहन्तम्
verses.transliteration: aru.n turaM paruSha.n rUxavAchaM vAkkaNTakairvitudantaM manuShyAn | vidyAdalaxmIkatama.n janAnAM mukhe nibaddhAM nirR^iti.n vahantam
verses.translation: That worst of men is of harsh and wrathful speech, who pierceth the vitals of others with wordy thorns, beareth hell in his tongue, and should ever be regarded as a dispenser of misery to men.
verses.hindi: तात ! मैं चिन्तासे जलता हुआ अभीतक जग रहा हूँ। मेरे लिये जो कल्याणकी बात समझो, वह कहो; क्योंकि हमलोगोंमें तुम्हीं धर्म और अर्थके ज्ञानमें निपुण हो
verses.wordMeaning: That worst of men is of harsh and wrathful speech, who pierceth the vitals of others with wordy thorns, beareth hell in his tongue, and should ever be regarded as a dispenser of misery to men.
verses.commentary: Sense: That worst of men is of harsh and wrathful speech, who pierceth the vitals of others with wordy thorns, beareth hell in his tongue, and should ever be regarded as a dispenser of misery to men.

verses.sanskrit: परश्चेदेनमधिविध्येत बाणैर् भृशं सुतीक्ष्णैरनलार्क दीप्तैः । विरिच्यमानोऽप्यतिरिच्यमानो विद्यात्कविः सुकृतं मे दधाति
verses.transliteration: parashchedenamadhividhyeta bANair bhR^isha.n sutIxNairanalArka dIptaiH | virichyamAno.apyatirichyamAno vidyAtkaviH sukR^itaM me dadhAti
verses.translation: The man that is wise, pierced by another's wordy arrows, sharp-pointed and smarting like fire or the sun, should, even if deeply wounded and burning with pain, bear them patiently remembering that the slanderer's merits become his.
verses.hindi: संजय जबसे पाण्डवोंके यहाँसे लौटकर आया है, तबसे मेरे मनको पूर्ण शान्ति नहीं मिलती  सभी इन्द्रियाँ विकल हो रही हैं। कल वह क्या कहेगा, इसी बातकी मुझे इस समय बड़ी भारी चिन्ता हो रही है
verses.wordMeaning: The man that is wise, pierced by another's wordy arrows, sharp-pointed and smarting like fire or the sun, should, even if deeply wounded and burning with pain, bear them patiently remembering that the slanderer's merits become his.
verses.commentary: Sense: The man that is wise, pierced by another's wordy arrows, sharp-pointed and smarting like fire or the sun, should, even if deeply wounded and burning with pain, bear them patiently remembering that the slanderer's merits become his.

verses.sanskrit: यदि सन्तं सेवते यद्यसन्तं तपस्विनं यदि वा स्तेनमेव । वासो यथा रङ्ग वशं प्रयाति तथा स तेषां वशमभ्युपैति
verses.transliteration: yadi santa.n sevate yadyasantaM tapasvina.n yadi vA stenameva | vAso yathA ra~Nga vashaM prayAti tathA sa teShA.n vashamabhyupaiti
verses.translation: He that waiteth upon one that is good or upon one that is wicked, upon one that is possessed of ascetic merit or upon one that is a thief, soon taketh the colour from that companion of his, like a cloth from the dye in which it is soaked.
verses.hindi: है. विदुरनीति विदुरजी बोले---राजन्‌ ! जिसका बलबानके साथ विसेध हो गया है उस साधनहीन दुर्बल मनुष्यको, जिसका सब कुछ हर लिया गया है उसको, कामीकों तथा चोरको रातमें जागनेका रोग छूग जाता है
verses.wordMeaning: He that waiteth upon one that is good or upon one that is wicked, upon one that is possessed of ascetic merit or upon one that is a thief, soon taketh the colour from that companion of his, like a cloth from the dye in which it is soaked.
verses.commentary: Sense: He that waiteth upon one that is good or upon one that is wicked, upon one that is possessed of ascetic merit or upon one that is a thief, soon taketh the colour from that companion of his, like a cloth from the dye in which it is soaked.

verses.sanskrit: वादं तु यो न प्रवदेन्न वादयेद् यो नाहतः प्रतिहन्यान्न घातयेत् । यो हन्तुकामस्य न पापमिच्छेत् तस्मै देवाः स्पृहयन्त्यागताय
verses.transliteration: vAda.n tu yo na pravadenna vAdayed.h yo nAhataH pratihanyAnna ghAtayet | yo hantukAmasya na pApamichChet.h tasmai devAH spR^ihayantyAgatAya
verses.translation: The very gods desire his company, who, stung with reproach, returneth it not himself nor causeth others to return it, or who being struck doth not himself return the blow nor causeth other to do it, and who wisheth not the slightest injury to him that injureth him.
verses.hindi: धृतराष्ट्रने कहा--मैं तुम्हारे धर्मयुक्त तथा कल्याण करनेवाले सुन्दर जचन सुनना चाहता हूँ, क्योंकि इस राजर्षिवंशमें. केवल तुम्हीं विद्वानोंके भी माननीय हो
verses.wordMeaning: The very gods desire his company, who, stung with reproach, returneth it not himself nor causeth others to return it, or who being struck doth not himself return the blow nor causeth other to do it, and who wisheth not the slightest injury to him that injureth him.
verses.commentary: Sense: The very gods desire his company, who, stung with reproach, returneth it not himself nor causeth others to return it, or who being struck doth not himself return the blow nor causeth other to do it, and who wisheth not the slightest injury to him that injureth him.

verses.sanskrit: अव्याहृतं व्याहृताच्छ्रेय आहुः सत्यं वदेद्व्याहृतं तद्द्वितीयम् । प्रियंवदेद्व्याहृतं तत्तृतीयं धर्म्यं वदेद्व्याहृतं तच्चतुर्थम्
verses.transliteration: avyAhR^ita.n vyAhR^itAchChreya AhuH satya.n vadedvyAhR^ita.n taddvitIyam | priya.nvadedvyAhR^ita.n tattR^itIyaM dharmya.n vadedvyAhR^ita.n tachchaturtham
verses.translation: Silence, it is said, is better than speech, if speak you must, then it is better to say the truth; if truth is to be said, it is better to say what is agreeable; and if what is agreeable is to be said, then it is better to say what is consistent with morality.
verses.hindi: आप धर्मात्मा और धर्मके जानकार होते हुए भी आँखोंसे अन्धे होनेके कारण उन्हें पहचान न सके, इसीसे उनके अत्यन्त विपरीत हो गये और उन्हें राज्यका भाग देनेमें आप्रकी सम्मति नहीं हुई
verses.wordMeaning: Silence, it is said, is better than speech, if speak you must, then it is better to say the truth; if truth is to be said, it is better to say what is agreeable; and if what is agreeable is to be said, then it is better to say what is consistent with morality.
verses.commentary: Sense: Silence, it is said, is better than speech, if speak you must, then it is better to say the truth; if truth is to be said, it is better to say what is agreeable; and if what is agreeable is to be said, then it is better to say what is consistent with morality.

verses.sanskrit: यादृशैः संविवदते यादृशांश् चोपसेवते । यादृगिच्छेच्च भवितुं तादृग्भवति पूरुषः
verses.transliteration: yAdR^ishaiH sa.nvivadate yAdR^ishAMsh chopasevate | yAdR^igichChechcha bhavitu.n tAdR^igbhavati pUruShaH
verses.translation: A man becometh exactly like him with whom he liveth, or like him whom he regardeth, or like that which he wisheth to be.
verses.hindi: आप दुर्योधन, शकुनि, कर्ण तथा दुःशासन-जैसे अयोग्य व्यक्तियोंपर राज्यका भार रखकर कैसे ऐश्वर्य-बृद्धि चाहते हैं ?
verses.wordMeaning: A man becometh exactly like him with whom he liveth, or like him whom he regardeth, or like that which he wisheth to be.
verses.commentary: Sense: A man becometh exactly like him with whom he liveth, or like him whom he regardeth, or like that which he wisheth to be.

verses.sanskrit: यतो यतो निवर्तते ततस्ततो विमुच्यते । निवर्तनाद्धि सर्वतो न वेत्ति दुःखमण्वपि
verses.transliteration: yato yato nivartate tatastato vimuchyate | nivartanAddhi sarvato na vetti duHkhamaNvapi
verses.translation: One is freed from those things from which one abstaineth, and if one abstaineth from everything he hath not to suffer even the least misery.
verses.hindi: अपने वास्तविक स्वरूपका ज्ञान, उद्योग, दुःख सहनेकी शक्ति और धर्ममें स्थिरता--ये गुण जिस मनुष्यको पुरुषार्थसे च्युत नहीं करते, वही पण्डित कहलाता है
verses.wordMeaning: One is freed from those things from which one abstaineth, and if one abstaineth from everything he hath not to suffer even the least misery.
verses.commentary: Sense: One is freed from those things from which one abstaineth, and if one abstaineth from everything he hath not to suffer even the least misery.

verses.sanskrit: न जीयते नोत जिगीषतेऽन्यान् न वैरक्कृच्चाप्रतिघातकश् च । निन्दा प्रशंसासु समस्वभावो न शोचते हृष्यति नैव चायम्
verses.transliteration: na jIyate nota jigIShate.anyAn.h na vairakkR^ichchApratighAtakash cha | nindA prasha.nsAsu samasvabhAvo na shochate hR^iShyati naiva chAyam
verses.translation: Such a man neither vanquisheth others, nor is vanquished by others. He never injureth nor opposeth others. He is unmoved by praise or blame. He neither grieveth nor exalteth in joy.
verses.hindi: जो अच्छे कर्मोका सेवन करता और बुरे कर्मोसि दूर रहता है, साथ ही जो आस्तिक और श्रद्धालु है, उसके वे सदगुण पण्डित होनेके लक्षण हैं
verses.wordMeaning: Such a man neither vanquisheth others, nor is vanquished by others. He never injureth nor opposeth others. He is unmoved by praise or blame. He neither grieveth nor exalteth in joy.
verses.commentary: Sense: Such a man neither vanquisheth others, nor is vanquished by others. He never injureth nor opposeth others. He is unmoved by praise or blame. He neither grieveth nor exalteth in joy.

verses.sanskrit: भावमिच्छति सर्वस्य नाभावे कुरुते मतिम् । सत्यवादी मृदुर्दान्तो यः स उत्तमपूरुषः
verses.transliteration: bhAvamichChati sarvasya nAbhAve kurute matim | satyavAdI mR^idurdAnto yaH sa uttamapUruShaH
verses.translation: That man is regarded as the first of his species who wisheth for the prosperity of all and never setteth his heart on the misery of others, who is truthful in speech, humble in behaviour, and hath all his passions under control.
verses.hindi: क्रोध, हर्ष, गर्व, लज्जा, उद्दण्डता तथा अपनेको पूज्य समझना---ये भाव जिसको पुरुषार्थसे भ्रष्ट नहीं करते, वही पण्डित कहलाता है
verses.wordMeaning: That man is regarded as the first of his species who wisheth for the prosperity of all and never setteth his heart on the misery of others, who is truthful in speech, humble in behaviour, and hath all his passions under control.
verses.commentary: Sense: That man is regarded as the first of his species who wisheth for the prosperity of all and never setteth his heart on the misery of others, who is truthful in speech, humble in behaviour, and hath all his passions under control.

verses.sanskrit: नानर्थकं सान्त्वयति प्रतिज्ञाय ददाति च । राद्धापराद्धे जानाति यः स मध्यमपूरुषः
verses.transliteration: nAnarthaka.n sAntvayati pratij~nAya dadAti cha | rAddhAparAddhe jAnAti yaH sa madhyamapUruShaH
verses.translation: That man is regarded as a mediocre in goodness who never consoleth others by saying what is not true; who giveth having promised; and who keepeth an eye over the weakness of others. ऽ
verses.hindi: दूसरे लोग जिसके कर्तव्य, सलाह और पहलेसे किये हुए विचारको नहीं जानते, बल्कि काम पूरा होनेपर ही जानते हैं, वही पण्डित कहलाता है
verses.wordMeaning: That man is regarded as a mediocre in goodness who never consoleth others by saying what is not true; who giveth having promised; and who keepeth an eye over the weakness of others. ऽ
verses.commentary: Sense: That man is regarded as a mediocre in goodness who never consoleth others by saying what is not true; who giveth having promised; and who keepeth an eye over the weakness of others. ऽ

verses.sanskrit: दुःशासनस्तूपहन्ता न शास्ता नावर्तते मन्युवशात्कृतघ्नः । न कस्य चिन्मित्रमथो दुरात्मा कलाश्चैता अधमस्येह पुंसः
verses.transliteration: duHshAsanastUpahantA na shAstA nAvartate manyuvashAtkR^itaghnaH | na kasya chinmitramatho durAtmA kalAshchaitA adhamasyeha pu.nsaH
verses.translation: These, however, are the indications of a bad man, viz., incapacity to be controlled; liability to be afflicted by dangers; proneness to give way to wrath, ungratefulness; inability to become another's friend, and wickedness of heart.
verses.hindi: जिसकी लौकिक बुद्धि धर्म और अर्थका ही अनुसरण करती है और जो भोगको छोड़कर पुरुषार्थका ही वरण करता है वही पण्डित कहछाता है ॥ २५॥ अथाझक्ति चिकीर्षन्ति यथाशक्ति च कुर्वते। न किझ्निदवमन्यन्ते नराः पण्डितबुद्धयः॥ २६ ॥ विवेकपूर्ण बुद्धिवालें पुरुष शक्तिके अनुसार काम करनेकी इच्छा रखते हैं और करते भी हैं तथा किसी वस्तुको तुच्छ समझकर उसकी अंवहेलना नहीं करते ॥ २६॥ क्षिप्र॑ विजानाति चिरे श्रूणोति विज्ञाय चार्थ भजते न कामात्‌। नासम्पृष्टो. व्युपयुडनक्ते . परार्थे तत्त. प्रज्ञानं प्रथर्म पण्डितस्थ
verses.wordMeaning: These, however, are the indications of a bad man, viz., incapacity to be controlled; liability to be afflicted by dangers; proneness to give way to wrath, ungratefulness; inability to become another's friend, and wickedness of heart.
verses.commentary: Sense: These, however, are the indications of a bad man, viz., incapacity to be controlled; liability to be afflicted by dangers; proneness to give way to wrath, ungratefulness; inability to become another's friend, and wickedness of heart.

verses.sanskrit: न श्रद्दधाति कल्याणं परेभ्योऽप्यात्मशङ्कितः । निराकरोति मित्राणि यो वै सोऽधम पूरुषः
verses.transliteration: na shraddadhAti kalyANaM parebhyo.apyAtmasha~NkitaH | nirAkaroti mitrANi yo vai so.adhama pUruShaH
verses.translation: He too is the worst of men, who is dissatisfied with any good that may come to him from others who is suspicious of his own self, and who driveth away from himself all his true friends.
verses.hindi: पण्डितोंकी-सी बुद्धि रखनेवाले मनुष्य दुर्लभ वस्तुकी कामना नहीं करते, खोयी हुईं वस्तुके विषयमें शोक करना नहीं च्वाहते और विपत्तिमें पड़कर घबराते नहीं हैं
verses.wordMeaning: He too is the worst of men, who is dissatisfied with any good that may come to him from others who is suspicious of his own self, and who driveth away from himself all his true friends.
verses.commentary: Sense: He too is the worst of men, who is dissatisfied with any good that may come to him from others who is suspicious of his own self, and who driveth away from himself all his true friends.

verses.sanskrit: उत्तमानेव सेवेत प्राप्ते काले तु मध्यमान् । अधमांस्तु न सेवेत य इच्छेच्छ्रेय आत्मनः
verses.transliteration: uttamAneva seveta prApte kAle tu madhyamAn | adhamA.nstu na seveta ya ichChechChreya AtmanaH
verses.translation: He that desireth prosperity to himself, should wait upon them that are good, and at times upon them that are indifferent, but never upon them that are bad.
verses.hindi: भरतकुल-भूषण ! पण्डितजन श्रेष्ठ क्मोंमें रुचि रखते हैं, उन्नतिके कार्य करते हैं तथा भलाई करनेवाल्टोमें दोष नहीं निकालते हैं
verses.wordMeaning: He that desireth prosperity to himself, should wait upon them that are good, and at times upon them that are indifferent, but never upon them that are bad.
verses.commentary: Sense: He that desireth prosperity to himself, should wait upon them that are good, and at times upon them that are indifferent, but never upon them that are bad.

verses.sanskrit: प्राप्नोति वै वित्तमसद्बलेन नित्योत्थानात्प्रज्ञया पौरुषेण । न त्वेव सम्यग्लभते प्रशंसां न वृत्तमाप्नोति महाकुलानाम्
verses.transliteration: prApnoti vai vittamasadbalena nityotthAnAtpraj~nayA pauruSheNa | na tveva samyaglabhate prasha.nsAM na vR^ittamApnoti mahAkulAnAm
verses.translation: He that is wicked, earneth wealth, it is true, by putting forth his strength, by constant effort, by intelligence, and by prowess, but he can never win honest fame, nor can he acquire the virtues and manners of high families (in any of which he may be born).'
verses.hindi: जो सम्पूर्ण भौतिक पदार्थोकी असंल्तियतका ज्ञान रखनेवाला, सब कार्येकि करनेका ढंग जाननेवाल्य तथा ममुष्योंमें सबसे बढ़कर उपायका जानकार है, वही मनुष्य पण्डित कहलाता है
verses.wordMeaning: He that is wicked, earneth wealth, it is true, by putting forth his strength, by constant effort, by intelligence, and by prowess, but he can never win honest fame, nor can he acquire the virtues and manners of high families (in any of which he may be born).'
verses.commentary: Sense: He that is wicked, earneth wealth, it is true, by putting forth his strength, by constant effort, by intelligence, and by prowess, but he can never win honest fame, nor can he acquire the virtues and manners of high families (in any of which he may be born).'

verses.sanskrit: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच । महाकुलानां स्पृहयन्ति देवा धर्मार्थवृद्धाश्च बहुश्रुताश् च । पृच्छामि त्वां विदुर प्रश्नमेतं भवन्ति वै कानि महाकुलानि
verses.transliteration: dhR^itarAShTra uvAcha | mahAkulAnA.n spR^ihayanti devA dharmArthavR^iddhAshcha bahushrutAsh cha | pR^ichChAmi tvA.n vidura prashnametaM bhavanti vai kAni mahAkulAni
verses.translation: "Dhritarashtra said, 'The gods, they that regard both virtue and profit without swerving from either, and they that are possessed of great learning, express a liking for high families. I ask thee, O Vidura, this question,--what are those families that are called high?'
verses.hindi: जिसकी वाणी कहीं रुकती नहीं, जो विचित्र छंगसे बातचीत करता है, तर्कमें निपण और प्रतिभाशाली हैं तथा जो ग्रन्थके तात्पर्यको ज्ीघ्र बता सकता है, बही पण्डित कहलाता है
verses.wordMeaning: "Dhritarashtra said, 'The gods, they that regard both virtue and profit without swerving from either, and they that are possessed of great learning, express a liking for high families. I ask thee, O Vidura, this question,--what are those families that are called high?'
verses.commentary: Sense: "Dhritarashtra said, 'The gods, they that regard both virtue and profit without swerving from either, and they that are possessed of great learning, express a liking for high families. I ask thee, O Vidura, this question,--what are those families that are called high?'

verses.sanskrit: विदुर उवाच । तमो दमो ब्रह्मवित्त्वं वितानाः पुण्या विवाहाः सततान्न दानम् । येष्वेवैते सप्तगुणा भवन्ति सम्यग्वृत्तास्तानि महाकुलानि
verses.transliteration: vidura uvAcha | tamo damo brahmavittva.n vitAnAH puNyA vivAhAH satatAnna dAnam | yeShvevaite saptaguNA bhavanti samyagvR^ittAstAni mahAkulAni
verses.translation: "Vidura said, 'Asceticism, self-restraint, knowledge of the Vedas, sacrifices, pure marriages, and gifts of food,--those families in which these seven exist or are practised duly, are regarded as high. There are high families who deviate not from the right course whose deceased ancestors are never pained (by witnessing the wrong- doings of their descendants), who cheerfully practise all the virtues, who desire to enhance the pure fame of the line in which they are born, and who avoid every kind of falsehood.
verses.hindi: । बिना' पढ़े ही गर्ब करनेवाले, दरिद्र होकर भी बड़े-बड़े. मनंसूजे बाँधनेवालें और बिना काम किये ही धन पानेकी इच्छा रखनेवाले मनुष्यको पण्डितलोगं मूर्ख कहते हैं
verses.wordMeaning: "Vidura said, 'Asceticism, self-restraint, knowledge of the Vedas, sacrifices, pure marriages, and gifts of food,--those families in which these seven exist or are practised duly, are regarded as high.…
verses.commentary: Sense: "Vidura said, 'Asceticism, self-restraint, knowledge of the Vedas, sacrifices, pure marriages, and gifts of food,--those families in which these seven exist or are practised duly, are regarded as high.…

verses.sanskrit: येषां न वृत्तं व्यथते न योनिर् वृत्तप्रसादेन चरन्ति धर्मम् । ये कीर्तिमिच्छन्ति कुले विशिष्टां त्यक्तानृतास्तानि महाकुलानि
verses.transliteration: yeShAM na vR^itta.n vyathate na yonir vR^ittaprasAdena charanti dharmam | ye kIrtimichChanti kule vishiShTAM tyaktAnR^itAstAni mahAkulAni
verses.translation: "Vidura said, 'Asceticism, self-restraint, knowledge of the Vedas, sacrifices, pure marriages, and gifts of food,--those families in which these seven exist or are practised duly, are regarded as high. There are high families who deviate not from the right course whose deceased ancestors are never pained (by witnessing the wrong- doings of their descendants), who cheerfully practise all the virtues, who desire to enhance the pure fame of the line in which they are born, and who avoid every kind of falsehood.
verses.hindi: जो न चाहनेवाल्लॉंको चाहता है और चाहनेवालोंको त्याग देता है तथा जो अपनेसे बलवानके साथ बैर बाँधता है, उसे 'मूढ़ विचारका मनुष्य' कहते हैं
verses.wordMeaning: "Vidura said, 'Asceticism, self-restraint, knowledge of the Vedas, sacrifices, pure marriages, and gifts of food,--those families in which these seven exist or are practised duly, are regarded as high.…
verses.commentary: Sense: "Vidura said, 'Asceticism, self-restraint, knowledge of the Vedas, sacrifices, pure marriages, and gifts of food,--those families in which these seven exist or are practised duly, are regarded as high.…

verses.sanskrit: अनिज्ययाविवाहैर्श्च वेदस्योत्सादनेन च । कुलान्यकुलतां यान्ति धर्मस्यातिक्रमेण च
verses.transliteration: anijyayAvivAhairshcha vedasyotsAdanena cha | kulAnyakulatA.n yAnti dharmasyAtikrameNa cha
verses.translation: Families that are high, fall down and become low owing to the absence of sacrifices, impure marriages, abandonment of the Vedas, and violation of virtues.
verses.hindi: मूढ़ चित्तताला अधम मनुष्य बिना बुछाये ही भीतर चला आता है, बिना पूछे ही बहुत बोलता है तथा अविश्वसनीय मनुष्योंपर भी विश्वास करता है
verses.wordMeaning: Families that are high, fall down and become low owing to the absence of sacrifices, impure marriages, abandonment of the Vedas, and violation of virtues.
verses.commentary: Sense: Families that are high, fall down and become low owing to the absence of sacrifices, impure marriages, abandonment of the Vedas, and violation of virtues.

verses.sanskrit: देव द्रव्यविनाशेन ब्रह्म स्वहरणेन च । कुलान्यकुलतां यान्ति ब्राह्मणातिक्रमेण च
verses.transliteration: deva dravyavinAshena brahma svaharaNena cha | kulAnyakulatA.n yAnti brAhmaNAtikrameNa cha
verses.translation: Families that are high, fall down and become low owing to the destruction of properties of deities, robbing of the properties of brahmanas, and insults offered to Brahmanas. च
verses.hindi: स्वर्य दोषयुक्त बर्ताव करते हुए भी जो दूसरेपर उसके दोष बताकर आक्षेप करता है तथा जो असमर्थ होते हुए भी व्यर्थका क्रोध करता है, बह मनुष्य महामूर्ख है
verses.wordMeaning: Families that are high, fall down and become low owing to the destruction of properties of deities, robbing of the properties of brahmanas, and insults offered to Brahmanas. च
verses.commentary: Sense: Families that are high, fall down and become low owing to the destruction of properties of deities, robbing of the properties of brahmanas, and insults offered to Brahmanas. च

verses.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणानां परिभवात्परिवादाच्च भारत । कुलान्यकुलतां यान्ति न्यासापहरणेन च
verses.transliteration: brAhmaNAnAM paribhavAtparivAdAchcha bhArata | kulAnyakulatA.n yAnti nyAsApaharaNena cha
verses.translation: High families fall off and become low owing to their members disregarding or speaking ill of Brahmanas, or to the misappropriation, O Bharata, of what had been deposited with them by others.
verses.hindi: जो अपने बलको न समझकर बिना काम किये ही धर्म और अर्थसे विरुद्ध तथा न पानेयोग्य बस्तुकी इच्छा करता है, वहे पुरुष इस संसारमें 'मूढ़बुद्धि' कहलाता है
verses.wordMeaning: High families fall off and become low owing to their members disregarding or speaking ill of Brahmanas, or to the misappropriation, O Bharata, of what had been deposited with them by others.
verses.commentary: Sense: High families fall off and become low owing to their members disregarding or speaking ill of Brahmanas, or to the misappropriation, O Bharata, of what had been deposited with them by others.

verses.sanskrit: कुलानि समुपेतानि गोभिः पुरुषतोऽश्वतः । कुलसङ्ख्यां न गच्छन्ति यानि हीनानि वृत्ततः
verses.transliteration: kulAni samupetAni gobhiH puruShato.ashvataH | kulasa~NkhyAM na gachChanti yAni hInAni vR^ittataH
verses.translation: He, in our race, who slayeth Brahmanas, or entertaineth feelings of aversion towards them, or impedeth or otherwise injureth agriculture, doth not deserve to mix with us.
verses.hindi: मनुष्य अकेल्ग॑ पाप करता है और बहुत-से लोग उससे मौज उड़ाते हैं। मौज़ उड़ानेवाले तो छूट जाते हैं; पर उसका कर्ता ही दोषका भागी होता है
verses.wordMeaning: He, in our race, who slayeth Brahmanas, or entertaineth feelings of aversion towards them, or impedeth or otherwise injureth agriculture, doth not deserve to mix with us.
verses.commentary: Sense: He, in our race, who slayeth Brahmanas, or entertaineth feelings of aversion towards them, or impedeth or otherwise injureth agriculture, doth not deserve to mix with us.

verses.sanskrit: वृत्ततस्त्वविहीनानि कुलान्यल्पधनान्यपि । कुलसङ्ख्यां तु गच्छन्ति कर्षन्ति च मयद्यशः
verses.transliteration: vR^ittatastvavihInAni kulAnyalpadhanAnyapi | kulasa~NkhyA.n tu gachChanti karShanti cha mayadyashaH
verses.translation: Those families that are possessed of members, wealth and kine, are not regarded as families if they be wanting in good manners and conduct, while families wanting in wealth but distinguished by manners and good conduct are regarded as such and win great reputation.
verses.hindi: किसी धरनुर्धर वीरके द्वारा छोड़ा हुआ बाण सम्भव है एकको भी मारे या न मारें। मगर बुद्धिमानद्वारा प्रयुक्त की हुई बुद्धि राजाके साथ-साथ सम्पूर्ण राष्ट्रका विनाश कर सकती है
verses.wordMeaning: Those families that are possessed of members, wealth and kine, are not regarded as families if they be wanting in good manners and conduct, while families wanting in wealth but distinguished by manners and good conduct are regarded as such and win great reputation.
verses.commentary: Sense: Those families that are possessed of members, wealth and kine, are not regarded as families if they be wanting in good manners and conduct, while families wanting in wealth but distinguished by manners and good conduct are regarded as such and win great reputation.

verses.sanskrit: मा नः कुले वैरकृत्कश् चिदस्तु राजामात्यो मा परस्वापहारी । मित्रद्रोही नैकृतिकोऽनृती वा पूर्वाशी वा पितृदेवातिथिभ्यः
verses.transliteration: mA naH kule vairakR^itkash chidastu rAjAmAtyo mA parasvApahArI | mitradrohI naikR^itiko.anR^itI vA pUrvAshI vA pitR^idevAtithibhyaH
verses.translation: Let none in our race be a fomenter of quarrels, none serve a king as minister, none steal the wealth of others, none provoke intestine dissensions, none be deceitful or false in behaviour, and none eat before serving the Rishis, the gods, and guests.
verses.hindi: विषका रस एक. (पीनेवाले) को ही मारता है, शख्ब्रसे एकका ही वध होता है, किंतु मन्त्रका फूटना राष्ट्र और ग्रजाके साथ ही राजाका भी विनाश कर डालता है
verses.wordMeaning: Let none in our race be a fomenter of quarrels, none serve a king as minister, none steal the wealth of others, none provoke intestine dissensions, none be deceitful or false in behaviour, and none eat before serving the Rishis, the gods, and guests.
verses.commentary: Sense: Let none in our race be a fomenter of quarrels, none serve a king as minister, none steal the wealth of others, none provoke intestine dissensions, none be deceitful or false in behaviour, and none eat before serving the Rishis, the gods, and guests.

verses.sanskrit: यश्च नो ब्राह्मणं हन्याद्यश्च नो ब्राह्मणान्द्विषेत् । न नः स समितिं गच्छेद्यश्च नो निर्वपेत्कृषिम्
verses.transliteration: yashcha no brAhmaNa.n hanyAdyashcha no brAhmaNAndviShet | na naH sa samiti.n gachChedyashcha no nirvapetkR^iShim
verses.translation: He, in our race, who slayeth Brahmanas, or entertaineth feelings of aversion towards them, or impedeth or otherwise injureth agriculture, doth not deserve to mix with us.
verses.hindi: राज़न्‌ ! जैसे समुद्रके पार जानेके लिये नाव ही एकमात्र साधन हैं, उसी अकार स्वर्गके लिये सत्य ही एकमात्र सोपान है, दूसरा नहीं, किंतु आप इसे नहीं समझ रहे हैं
verses.wordMeaning: He, in our race, who slayeth Brahmanas, or entertaineth feelings of aversion towards them, or impedeth or otherwise injureth agriculture, doth not deserve to mix with us.
verses.commentary: Sense: He, in our race, who slayeth Brahmanas, or entertaineth feelings of aversion towards them, or impedeth or otherwise injureth agriculture, doth not deserve to mix with us.

verses.sanskrit: तृणानि भूमिरुदकं वाक्चतुर्थी च सूनृता । सतामेतानि गेहेषु नोच्छिद्यन्ते कदा चन
verses.transliteration: tR^iNAni bhUmirudaka.n vAkchaturthI cha sUnR^itA | satAmetAni geheShu nochChidyante kadA chana
verses.translation: Straw (for a seat), ground (for sitting upon), water (to wash the feet and face), and, fourthly sweet words,--these are never wanting in the houses of the good.
verses.hindi: किंतु क्षमाशील पुरुषका वह दोष नहीं मानना चाहिये; क्योंकि क्षमा बहुत बड़ा बल है। क्षमा असमर्थ मनुष्योंकां गुण तथा समर्थोका भूषण है
verses.wordMeaning: Straw (for a seat), ground (for sitting upon), water (to wash the feet and face), and, fourthly sweet words,--these are never wanting in the houses of the good.
verses.commentary: Sense: Straw (for a seat), ground (for sitting upon), water (to wash the feet and face), and, fourthly sweet words,--these are never wanting in the houses of the good.

verses.sanskrit: श्रद्धया परया राजन्नुपनीतानि सत्कृतिम् । प्रवृत्तानि महाप्राज्ञ धर्मिणां पुण्यकर्मणाम्
verses.transliteration: shraddhayA parayA rAjannupanItAni satkR^itim | pravR^ittAni mahAprAj~na dharmiNAM puNyakarmaNAm
verses.translation: Virtuous men devoted to the practice of righteous acts, when desirous of entertaining (guests), have these things ready for being offered with reverence.
verses.hindi: श्र विदुरनीति "कै के के अ  अटैक के कै है कै कफ कै है है जैक है कै है 3 कैप कम है कफ है४ ै ४ कै जैक के आज अैफे. इस जगतमें क्षमा वशीकरणंरूप है। भला, क्षमासे क्या नहीं सिद्ध होता ? जिसके हाथमें झान्तिरूपी तलवार है, उसका दुष्ट पुरुष क्या कर लेंगे ? ॥ ५५ ॥ अतृणे. पतितो. बहिः.. स्वयमेबोपश्ञाम्यति । अक्षमावान्‌ परे दोषेरात्मानं चैव . योजयेत्‌ ॥ ५८ ॥ तृणरहित स्थानमें गिरी हुई आग अपने-आप बुझ जाती है। क्षमाहीन पुरुष अपनेको' तथा दूसरेको भी दोष॒का भागी बना लेता है।॥ ५६ ॥ एको अथर्म: पर श्रेयः क्षमैका जझ्ञान्तिरुत्तमा । विद्येका परमा तृप्तिरहिंसेका सुखावहा
verses.wordMeaning: Virtuous men devoted to the practice of righteous acts, when desirous of entertaining (guests), have these things ready for being offered with reverence.
verses.commentary: Sense: Virtuous men devoted to the practice of righteous acts, when desirous of entertaining (guests), have these things ready for being offered with reverence.

verses.sanskrit: सूक्ष्मोऽपि भारं नृपते स्यन्दनो वै शक्तो वोढुं न तथान्ये महीजाः । एवं युक्ता भारसहा भवन्ति महाकुलीना न तथान्ये मनुष्याः
verses.transliteration: sUxmo.api bhAraM nR^ipate syandano vai shakto voDhuM na tathAnye mahIjAH | eva.n yuktA bhArasahA bhavanti mahAkulInA na tathAnye manuShyAH
verses.translation: As the Sandal tree, O king, though thin, is competent to bear weights which timbers of other trees (much thicker) cannot; so they that belong to high families are always able to bear the weight of great cares which ordinary men cannot.
verses.hindi: बिलमें रहनेवाले मेढक आदि जीवॉको जैसे साँप खा जातां है, उसी प्रकार यह पृथ्वी शत्रुसें बिरेध न करनेवाले राजां और परदेश-सेवन न करनेवाले ब्राह्ण--इन दोनोंको खा जाती है
verses.wordMeaning: As the Sandal tree, O king, though thin, is competent to bear weights which timbers of other trees (much thicker) cannot; so they that belong to high families are always able to bear the weight of great cares which ordinary men cannot.
verses.commentary: Sense: As the Sandal tree, O king, though thin, is competent to bear weights which timbers of other trees (much thicker) cannot; so they that belong to high families are always able to bear the weight of great cares which ordinary men cannot.

verses.sanskrit: न तन्मित्रं यस्य कोपाद्बिभेति यद्वा मित्रं शङ्कितेनोपचर्यम् । यस्मिन्मित्रे पितरीवाश्वसीत तद्वै मित्रं सङ्गतानीतराणि
verses.transliteration: na tanmitra.n yasya kopAdbibheti yadvA mitra.n sha~Nkitenopacharyam | yasminmitre pitarIvAshvasIta tadvai mitra.n sa~NgatAnItarANi
verses.translation: He is no friend whose anger inspireth fear, or who is to be waited upon with fear. He, however, on whom one can repose confidence as on a father, is a true friend. Other friendships are nominal connection.
verses.hindi: जरा भी कठोर न बोलना और दुष्ट पुरुषोंका आदर न करना--इन दो कर्मोको करनेवाला मनुष्य इस लछोकमें विशेष शोभा पाता है
verses.wordMeaning: He is no friend whose anger inspireth fear, or who is to be waited upon with fear. He, however, on whom one can repose confidence as on a father, is a true friend. Other friendships are nominal connection.
verses.commentary: Sense: He is no friend whose anger inspireth fear, or who is to be waited upon with fear. He, however, on whom one can repose confidence as on a father, is a true friend. Other friendships are nominal connection.

verses.sanskrit: यदि चेदप्यसम्बन्धो मित्रभावेन वर्तते । स एव बन्धुस्तन्मित्रं सा गतिस्तत्परायणम्
verses.transliteration: yadi chedapyasambandho mitrabhAvena vartate | sa eva bandhustanmitra.n sA gatistatparAyaNam
verses.translation: He that beareth himself as a friend, even though unconnected by birth of blood, is a true friend, a real refuge, and a protector.
verses.hindi: दूसरी स्त्रीद्वारा चाहे गये पुरुषकी कामना करनेवाल्ी स्त्रियाँ तथा दूसरोंके द्वारा पूजित मनुष्यका आदर करनेवाले पुरुष--ये दो प्रकारके लोग दूसरोंपर विश्वास करके चलनेवाले हैं
verses.wordMeaning: He that beareth himself as a friend, even though unconnected by birth of blood, is a true friend, a real refuge, and a protector.
verses.commentary: Sense: He that beareth himself as a friend, even though unconnected by birth of blood, is a true friend, a real refuge, and a protector.

verses.sanskrit: चलचित्तस्य वै पुंसो वृद्धाननुपसेवतः । पारिप्लवमतेर्नित्यमध्रुवो मित्र सङ्ग्रहः
verses.transliteration: chalachittasya vai pu.nso vR^iddhAnanupasevataH | pAriplavamaternityamadhruvo mitra sa~NgrahaH
verses.translation: He, whose heart is unsteady, or who doth not wait upon the aged, or who is of a restless disposition cannot make friends.
verses.hindi: दो ही अपने विपरीत कर्मके कारण शोभा नहीं पाते---अकर्मण्य गृहस्थ और ज्रपञ्ञमें छूगा हुआ संन्‍्यासी
verses.wordMeaning: He, whose heart is unsteady, or who doth not wait upon the aged, or who is of a restless disposition cannot make friends.
verses.commentary: Sense: He, whose heart is unsteady, or who doth not wait upon the aged, or who is of a restless disposition cannot make friends.

verses.sanskrit: चलचित्तमनात्मानमिन्द्रियाणां वशानुगम् । अर्थाः समतिवर्तन्ते हंसाः शुष्कं सरो यथा
verses.transliteration: chalachittamanAtmAnamindriyANA.n vashAnugam | arthAH samativartante ha.nsAH shuShka.n saro yathA
verses.translation: Success (in the attainment of objects) forsaketh the person whose heart is unsteady, or who hath no control over his mind, or who is a slave of his senses, like swans forsaking a tank whose waters have dried up.
verses.hindi: ॥ जो घनी होनेपर भी दान न दे और दरिद्र होनेपर भी कष्ट सहम न कर सके--इन दो ग्रकारके मनुष्योंकों गलेमें मजबूत पत्थर बाँधकर पानीमें डुबा देना चाहिये
verses.wordMeaning: Success (in the attainment of objects) forsaketh the person whose heart is unsteady, or who hath no control over his mind, or who is a slave of his senses, like swans forsaking a tank whose waters have dried up.
verses.commentary: Sense: Success (in the attainment of objects) forsaketh the person whose heart is unsteady, or who hath no control over his mind, or who is a slave of his senses, like swans forsaking a tank whose waters have dried up.

verses.sanskrit: अकस्मादेव कुप्यन्ति प्रसीदन्त्यनिमित्ततः । शीलमेतदसाधूनामभ्रं पारिप्लवं यथा
verses.transliteration: akasmAdeva kupyanti prasIdantyanimittataH | shIlametadasAdhUnAmabhraM pAriplava.n yathA
verses.translation: They that are of weak minds suddenly give way to anger and are gratified without sufficient cause; they are like clouds that are so inconstant.
verses.hindi: पुरुषश्रेष्ठ ! ये दो प्रकारके पुरुष सूर्यमण्डलको भेदकर ऊर्ध्व॑गतिको प्राप्त होते हैं---योगयुक्त संन्यासी और संग्ममें लोहा लेते हुए मारा गया योद्धा
verses.wordMeaning: They that are of weak minds suddenly give way to anger and are gratified without sufficient cause; they are like clouds that are so inconstant.
verses.commentary: Sense: They that are of weak minds suddenly give way to anger and are gratified without sufficient cause; they are like clouds that are so inconstant.

verses.sanskrit: सत्कृताश्च कृतार्थाश्च मित्राणां न भवन्ति ये । तान्मृतानपि क्रव्यादाः कृतघ्नान्नोपभुञ्जते
verses.transliteration: satkR^itAshcha kR^itArthAshcha mitrANAM na bhavanti ye | tAnmR^itAnapi kravyAdAH kR^itaghnAnnopabhu~njate
verses.translation: The very birds of prey abstain from touching the dead bodies of those who having been served and benefited by friends, show ingratitude to the latter.
verses.hindi: राजन्‌  तीन ही धनके अधिकारी नहीं माने जाते--ख्त्री, पुत्र तथा दास  ये जो कुछ कमाते हैं, वह घन उसीका होता है जिसके अधीन ये रहते हैं
verses.wordMeaning: The very birds of prey abstain from touching the dead bodies of those who having been served and benefited by friends, show ingratitude to the latter.
verses.commentary: Sense: The very birds of prey abstain from touching the dead bodies of those who having been served and benefited by friends, show ingratitude to the latter.

verses.sanskrit: अर्थयेदेव मित्राणि सति वासति वा धने । नानर्थयन्विजानाति मित्राणां सारफल्गुताम्
verses.transliteration: arthayedeva mitrANi sati vAsati vA dhane | nAnarthayanvijAnAti mitrANA.n sAraphalgutAm
verses.translation: Beest thou poor or beest thou rich, thou shouldst honour thy friends. Until some service is asked, the sincerity or otherwise of friends cannot be known.
verses.hindi: दूसरेके धनका .हरण, दूसरेकी स्त्रीका संसर्ग तथा सुहृद्‌ मित्रका परित्याग--ये तीनों ही दोष नाश करनेवाले होते हैं
verses.wordMeaning: Beest thou poor or beest thou rich, thou shouldst honour thy friends. Until some service is asked, the sincerity or otherwise of friends cannot be known.
verses.commentary: Sense: Beest thou poor or beest thou rich, thou shouldst honour thy friends. Until some service is asked, the sincerity or otherwise of friends cannot be known.

verses.sanskrit: सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते रूपं सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते बलम् । सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते ज्ञानं सन्तापाद्व्याधिमृच्छति
verses.transliteration: santApAdbhrashyate rUpa.n santApAdbhrashyate balam | santApAdbhrashyate j~nAna.n santApAdvyAdhimR^ichChati
verses.translation: Sorrow killeth beauty; sorrow killeth strength; sorrow killeth the understanding; and sorrow bringeth on disease.
verses.hindi: । काम, क्रोध- और छोभ---गे आत्माक्ा नाश करनेवाले नरकके तीन दरवाजे हैं, अतः इन तीमोंकों त्याग देना चाहिये।
verses.wordMeaning: Sorrow killeth beauty; sorrow killeth strength; sorrow killeth the understanding; and sorrow bringeth on disease.
verses.commentary: Sense: Sorrow killeth beauty; sorrow killeth strength; sorrow killeth the understanding; and sorrow bringeth on disease.

verses.sanskrit: अनवाप्यं च शोकेन शरीरं चोपतप्यते । अमित्राश्च प्रहृष्यन्ति मा स्म शोके मनः कृथाः
verses.transliteration: anavApya.n cha shokena sharIraM chopatapyate | amitrAshcha prahR^iShyanti mA sma shoke manaH kR^ithAH
verses.translation: Grief, instead of helping the acquisition of his object, drieth up the body, and maketh one's foes glad. Therefore, do not yield to grief.
verses.hindi: भक्त, सेवक तथा मैं आपका ही हूँ, ऐसा कहनेवाले--इन तीन प्रकारके शरणागत मनुष्योंकों संकट पड़नेपर भी नहीं छोड़ना चाहिये
verses.wordMeaning: Grief, instead of helping the acquisition of his object, drieth up the body, and maketh one's foes glad. Therefore, do not yield to grief.
verses.commentary: Sense: Grief, instead of helping the acquisition of his object, drieth up the body, and maketh one's foes glad. Therefore, do not yield to grief.

verses.sanskrit: पुनर्नरो म्रियते जायते च पुनर्नरो हीयते वर्धते पुनः । पुनर्नरो याचति याच्यते च पुनर्नरः शोचति शोच्यते पुनः
verses.transliteration: punarnaro mriyate jAyate cha punarnaro hIyate vardhate punaH | punarnaro yAchati yAchyate cha punarnaraH shochati shochyate punaH
verses.translation: Men repeatedly die and are reborn; repeatedly they wither away and grow; repeatedly they ask others for help, and they themselves are asked for help; repeatedly they lament and are lamented.
verses.hindi: थोड़ी बुद्धिवाले, दीर्घसूत्री, जल्दबाज और स्तुति करनेवाले ल्तेंगोंके साथ गुप्त सलाह नहीं करनी चाहिये--ये चारों महाबल्ी राजाके लिये त्यागने योग्य बताये गये हैं। विद्वान्‌ पुरुष ऐसे ल्लोेगोंको पहचान ले
verses.wordMeaning: Men repeatedly die and are reborn; repeatedly they wither away and grow; repeatedly they ask others for help, and they themselves are asked for help; repeatedly they lament and are lamented.
verses.commentary: Sense: Men repeatedly die and are reborn; repeatedly they wither away and grow; repeatedly they ask others for help, and they themselves are asked for help; repeatedly they lament and are lamented.

verses.sanskrit: सुखं च दुःखं च भवाभवौ च लाभालाभौ मरणं जीवितं च । पर्यायशः सर्वमिह स्पृशन्ति तस्माद्धीरो नैव हृष्येन्न शोचेत्
verses.transliteration: sukha.n cha duHkhaM cha bhavAbhavau cha lAbhAlAbhau maraNa.n jIvitaM cha | paryAyashaH sarvamiha spR^ishanti tasmAddhIro naiva hR^iShyenna shochet
verses.translation: Happiness and misery, plenty and want, gain and loss, life and death, are shared by all in due order. Therefore, he that is self- controlled should neither exult in joy nor repine in sorrow.
verses.hindi: । तात ! गृहस्थ-धर्ममें स्थित लक्ष्मीबानूं आपके घरमें चार अकारके मनुष्योंको सदा रहना चाहिये---अपने कुटुम्बका बूढ़ा, संकटमें पड़ा हुआ उच्च कुलका मनुष्य, धनहीन मित्र और बिना सन्‍्तानकी बहिन
verses.wordMeaning: Happiness and misery, plenty and want, gain and loss, life and death, are shared by all in due order. Therefore, he that is self- controlled should neither exult in joy nor repine in sorrow.
verses.commentary: Sense: Happiness and misery, plenty and want, gain and loss, life and death, are shared by all in due order. Therefore, he that is self- controlled should neither exult in joy nor repine in sorrow.

verses.sanskrit: चलानि हीमानि षडिन्द्रियाणि तेषां यद्यद्वर्तते यत्र यत्र । ततस्ततः स्रवते बुद्धिरस्य छिद्रोद कुम्भादिव नित्यमम्भः
verses.transliteration: chalAni hImAni ShaDindriyANi teShA.n yadyadvartate yatra yatra | tatastataH sravate buddhirasya Chidroda kumbhAdiva nityamambhaH
verses.translation: The six senses are always restless. Through the most predominant one amongst them one's understanding escapeth in proportion to the strength it assumes, like water from a pot through its holes.'
verses.hindi: महाराज ! इन्द्रके पूछनेपर उनसे बृहस्पतिजीने जिन चारोंको तत्काल / ; ॥॥ श्च विदुरनीति री 'फल देनेवाल्ग बताया था, उन्हें आप मुझसे सुनिये---
verses.wordMeaning: The six senses are always restless. Through the most predominant one amongst them one's understanding escapeth in proportion to the strength it assumes, like water from a pot through its holes.'
verses.commentary: Sense: The six senses are always restless. Through the most predominant one amongst them one's understanding escapeth in proportion to the strength it assumes, like water from a pot through its holes.'

verses.sanskrit: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच । तनुरुच्छः शिखी राजा मिथ्योपचरितो मया । मन्दानां मम पुत्राणां युद्धेनान्तं करिष्यति
verses.transliteration: dhR^itarAShTra uvAcha | tanuruchChaH shikhI rAjA mithyopacharito mayA | mandAnAM mama putrANA.n yuddhenAnta.n kariShyati
verses.translation: "Dhritarashtra said, 'King Yudhishthira who is like a flame of fire, has been deceived by me.
verses.hindi: देवताओंका सह्जूल्प, बुद्धिमानोंक़ा प्रभाव, विद्वांनोंकी मम्नता और पापियोंका विनाहा
verses.wordMeaning: "Dhritarashtra said, 'King Yudhishthira who is like a flame of fire, has been deceived by me.
verses.commentary: Sense: "Dhritarashtra said, 'King Yudhishthira who is like a flame of fire, has been deceived by me.

verses.sanskrit: नित्योद्विग्नमिदं सर्वं नित्योद्विग्नमिदं मनः । यत्तत्पदमनुद्विग्नं तन्मे वद महामते
verses.transliteration: nityodvignamida.n sarvaM nityodvignamidaM manaH | yattatpadamanudvigna.n tanme vada mahAmate
verses.translation: He will surely exterminate in battle all my wicked sons. Everything, therefore, seems to me to be fraught with danger, and my mind is full of anxiety, O thou of great intelligence, tell me such words as may dispel my anxiety.'
verses.hindi: चार कर्म भयकों दूर॑ करनेवाले हैं; किन्तु वें ही यदि ठीक तरहसे सम्पादित न हों तो भय ग्रदांन करते हैं। वे कर्म हैं--आदरके साथ अमिहोत्र, आदरपूर्वक मौनका पालन, आदरपूर्वक स्वाध्याय और आंदरके साथ यज्ञका अनुष्ठान
verses.wordMeaning: He will surely exterminate in battle all my wicked sons. Everything, therefore, seems to me to be fraught with danger, and my mind is full of anxiety, O thou of great intelligence, tell me such words as may dispel my anxiety.'
verses.commentary: Sense: He will surely exterminate in battle all my wicked sons. Everything, therefore, seems to me to be fraught with danger, and my mind is full of anxiety, O thou of great intelligence, tell me such words as may dispel my anxiety.'

verses.sanskrit: विदुर उवाच । नान्यत्र विद्या तपसोर्नान्यत्रेन्द्रिय निग्रहात् । नान्यत्र लोभसन्त्यागाच्छान्तिं पश्याम तेऽनघ
verses.transliteration: vidura uvAcha | nAnyatra vidyA tapasornAnyatrendriya nigrahAt | nAnyatra lobhasantyAgAchChAntiM pashyAma te.anagha
verses.translation: "Vidura said, 'O sinless one, in nothing else than knowledge and asceticism, in nothing else than restraining the senses, in nothing else than complete abandonment of avarice, do I see thy good.
verses.hindi: भरतश्रेष्ठ । पिता, माता, अम्रि, आत्मा और गुरु--मनुष्यको इन पाँच अम्रियोंकी बड़े यत्रसे सेवा करनी चाहिये
verses.wordMeaning: "Vidura said, 'O sinless one, in nothing else than knowledge and asceticism, in nothing else than restraining the senses, in nothing else than complete abandonment of avarice, do I see thy good.
verses.commentary: Sense: "Vidura said, 'O sinless one, in nothing else than knowledge and asceticism, in nothing else than restraining the senses, in nothing else than complete abandonment of avarice, do I see thy good.

verses.sanskrit: बुद्ध्या भयं प्रणुदति तपसा विन्दते महत् । गुरुशुश्रूषया ज्ञानं शान्तिं त्यागेन विन्दति
verses.transliteration: buddhyA bhayaM praNudati tapasA vindate mahat | gurushushrUShayA j~nAna.n shAnti.n tyAgena vindati
verses.translation: Fear is dispelled by self-knowledge; by asceticism one winneth what is great and valuable; by waiting upon superiors learning is acquired; and peace is gained by self- restraint.
verses.hindi: देवता, पितर, मनुष्य, संन्यासीं और अतिथि--इन पाँचोंकी पूजा करनेवाला मनुष्य शुद्ध यश प्राप्त करता है
verses.wordMeaning: Fear is dispelled by self-knowledge; by asceticism one winneth what is great and valuable; by waiting upon superiors learning is acquired; and peace is gained by self- restraint.
verses.commentary: Sense: Fear is dispelled by self-knowledge; by asceticism one winneth what is great and valuable; by waiting upon superiors learning is acquired; and peace is gained by self- restraint.

verses.sanskrit: अनाश्रिता दानपुण्यं वेद पुण्यमनाश्रिताः । रागद्वेषविनिर्मुक्ता विचरन्तीह मोक्षिणः
verses.transliteration: anAshritA dAnapuNya.n veda puNyamanAshritAH | rAgadveShavinirmuktA vicharantIha moxiNaH
verses.translation: They that desire salvation without having acquired the merit attainable by gifts, or that which is attainable by practising the ritual of the Vedas, do not sojourn through life, freed from anger and aversion.
verses.hindi: पाँच ज्ञानेन्द्रियोंवाले पुरुषकी यदि एक भी इन्द्रिय छिद्र (दोष) युक्त हों जाय तो उससे उसकी बुद्धि इस प्रकार बाहर निकल जाती है, जैसे महझकके छेदसे पानी
verses.wordMeaning: They that desire salvation without having acquired the merit attainable by gifts, or that which is attainable by practising the ritual of the Vedas, do not sojourn through life, freed from anger and aversion.
verses.commentary: Sense: They that desire salvation without having acquired the merit attainable by gifts, or that which is attainable by practising the ritual of the Vedas, do not sojourn through life, freed from anger and aversion.

verses.sanskrit: स्वधीतस्य सुयुद्धस्य सुकृतस्य च कर्मणः । तपसश्च सुतप्तस्य तस्यान्ते सुखमेधते
verses.transliteration: svadhItasya suyuddhasya sukR^itasya cha karmaNaH | tapasashcha sutaptasya tasyAnte sukhamedhate
verses.translation: The happiness that may be derived from a judicious course of study, from a battle fought virtuously, from ascetic austerities performed rigidly, always increaseth at the end.
verses.hindi: । ऐश्वर्य या उन्नति चाहनेवाले पुरुषोंको नींद, तन्द्रा (ऊँघना), डर, क्रोध, आलस्य तथा दीर्घसूत्रता (जल्दी हो जानेबाले काममें अधिक देर लगानेंकी आदत) --इन छः दुर्गुणोंको त्याग देना चाहिये
verses.wordMeaning: The happiness that may be derived from a judicious course of study, from a battle fought virtuously, from ascetic austerities performed rigidly, always increaseth at the end.
verses.commentary: Sense: The happiness that may be derived from a judicious course of study, from a battle fought virtuously, from ascetic austerities performed rigidly, always increaseth at the end.

verses.sanskrit: स्वास्तीर्णानि शयनानि प्रपन्ना न वै भिन्ना जातु निद्रां लभन्ते । न स्त्रीषु राजन्रतिमाप्नुवन्ति न मागधैः स्तूयमाना न सूतैः
verses.transliteration: svAstIrNAni shayanAni prapannA na vai bhinnA jAtu nidrA.n labhante | na strIShu rAjanratimApnuvanti na mAgadhaiH stUyamAnA na sUtaiH
verses.translation: They that are no longer in peace with their relatives, obtain no steep even if they have recourse to well-made beds; nor do they, O king, derive any pleasure from women, or the laudatory hymns of bards and eulogists.
verses.hindi: मनुष्यको कभी भी सत्य, दान, कर्मण्यता, अनसूया (गुणोंमें दोष श्८ विंदुरनीति कल कै केक केक के कैफ कै  के कफ अं जे कै कै क कै फै है के केक कै अे क े जे है फै औ के कै औ जज फेक कै है दिखानेकी प्रंवृत्तका अभाव) , क्षमा तथा घैर्य--इन छः गुणोंका त्याग नहीं करना चाहिये
